meta.purpose: Second sources for SINGLE-SOURCE modern (1820+) facts in Historian-owned data/eras files and the Southern Region 1972–83 sub-layer. The Analyst made no edits to those files.
meta.rules: Fatality figures and control-of-territory claims excluded. Quotes <=25 words.

new_second_sources.claim: Addis Ababa Agreement 1972; Southern Region established by the Regional Self-Government Act

new_source.citation: Johnson, Douglas H. The Root Causes of Sudan's Civil Wars, "Appendix: Chronology of Events". Cambridge University Press / James Currey (African Issues).
new_source.quote: embodied in the Regional Self-Government Act (3 March); Southern Region established under an interim government led by ... Abel Alier

new_second_sources.note: Agrees that the Act created the Southern Region in March 1972. Ratification date differs: Johnson has "ratified in Khartoum by Nimairi & Lagu (2 March)", but the UN text only fixes ratification for 12 Mar 1972. Badge CONTESTED if a ratification date is displayed.

new_second_sources.field: Southern Region end 1983 / Republican Order No. 1
new_second_sources.claim: Republican Order No. 1 (June 1983) abrogated the Addis Ababa arrangements; the South was divided into three regions
new_second_sources.existing_source: Sidahmed & Sidahmed, Sudan (Routledge 2005), Chronology: "June Nimeiri issues Republican order No. 1"

new_source.citation: Salman M. A. Salman, "South Sudan Road to Independence: Broken Promises and Lost Opportunities", Global Business & Development Law Journal 26 (2013), University of the Pacific McGeorge
new_source.quote: on June 5, 1983 issued Republican Order No. 1, establishing three regions in the place of the one region under the Self-Government Act

new_second_sources.note: Agrees with June 1983 and adds the day, 5 June. The primary text of the Order is still unread. Suggest the date read "5 Jun 1983 (Salman 2013)" with the existing chronology as corroboration.
